raw_response:
I farm in Quzhou County, so I will stay with the system I trust most: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That fits my land, my labor, and the local weather better than chasing something fancy. I am 47, I know this rotation, and with a middle level of schooling I prefer crops I can manage steadily and on time rather than crops that need more market guessing or delicate field work. Wheat gives me a stable first harvest, and maize uses the summer heat and rain after wheat comes off. I will keep most of my land in this grain rotation, use improved or hybrid seed where it clearly pays, and manage fertilizer and water tightly because costs matter. I will plough before wheat where the straw load is heavy so I can mix residue well, then use rotary tillage after wheat harvest for maize so I can plant quickly. I will not overwater, and I will spray only when field pressure is real, because yield comes from timing and field discipline, not from spending blindly. My goal is steady output, controlled cost, and low production risk.
